# Nxeon community Discord: server blueprint (mkt-036)

Status: DESIGN ONLY. Nothing in this document has been created on Discord, Disboard or top.gg. The owner (or a person the owner delegates) builds it by hand from this blueprint using the launch checklist in `docs/COMMUNITY-DISCORD-LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md`, and the listing text is in `docs/COMMUNITY-DISCORD-LISTING-COPY.md`.

Owner decision (growth batch, 2026-10-02): `change`. The owner's words: "We have a discord. However our discord community is super basic. I feel like it needs some work. Currently there are vulnerabilities, and it's just too basic. Needs more advancement."

So this is not a greenfield server. It is a rebuild of the community side, with the security problems designed out first.

## 1. What exists today, and why it must be split

Facts below come from the repo (`lib/discord*.ts`, `lib/settings.ts`) and the incident notes for 2026-09-05 and 2026-09-06.

- One Discord guild, "Nxeon Cloud", does three unrelated jobs at once: staff HQ and management, per-customer support ticket and live-chat channels (created by `lib/discord-bridge.ts`), and a public community area (Welcome, Community, Support self-help, Game Servers, Voice, Alerts).
- The bot ("Nxeon Support") is HTTP-only (Interactions Endpoint, REST). It is not a Gateway client, so it cannot moderate, welcome, or react to joins. It holds the Administrator permission.
- "Sign in with Discord" requests the `guilds.join` scope and adds every customer who signs up that way straight into that same guild (`lib/discord-auth.ts`, `app/api/discord/login/route.ts`). Customers are therefore auto-joined into the guild that contains staff and ticket channels.
- Customer badge roles (Verified, VPS Owner, Game Owner, Hosting, Partner) are synced from real account data by `lib/discord-roles.ts`. Staff roles (Owner, Admin, Manager, Staff, Customer Support) are assigned by hand.
- 2026-09-05: ticket and live-chat channels were visible to non-staff members because categories were created with no `@everyone` deny. Fixed in code and live. 2026-09-06: a narrower recurrence was reported (a fresh account saw one ticket channel name in the Suggested sidebar) and is recorded as unresolved.

### Vulnerability list this rebuild must close

| # | Weakness | Why it matters | Fix in this design |
|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | Community and customer tickets share one guild | Any permission slip exposes private support data; the 2026-09-05 leak happened exactly this way | Two guilds. Community is a new guild with NO ticket channels and NO customer data. Tickets stay in the existing guild, which becomes private (see section 3) |
| V2 | Auto-join of every Discord-signup customer into the support guild | Customers land in the staff guild by default | Owner decision D1: point auto-join at the community guild, and make the support guild invite-only. Needs a small code change, NOT made here |
| V3 | Bot has Administrator | A stolen bot token is full server takeover | Community guild bot set uses least-privilege roles (section 5). Support bot: replace Administrator with the specific permissions it uses (Manage Channels, Manage Roles, Send Messages, View Channel, Read Message History, Embed Links), tested on a spare guild first |
| V4 | No moderation layer (HTTP-only bot cannot see joins or messages) | Raids, scams, invite spam, token-grabber links | A real moderation bot plus Discord's own AutoMod (section 6). The HTTP bot stays out of the community |
| V5 | Basic setup: no verification level, no rules screen, no onboarding | Throwaway accounts can post immediately | Community feature on, rules screen, verification level, onboarding questions (sections 4 and 7) |
| V6 | Staff roles can be assigned in the Discord UI by anyone with Manage Roles | Role escalation | Only Owner holds Manage Roles; moderators get a capped role below the bot's role; 2FA required for every moderator (section 4) |
| V7 | Webhook and invite sprawl | Leaked webhook = posting as the server | Quarterly audit of webhooks, integrations and invites (checklist) |
| V8 | Open recurrence from 2026-09-06 is unexplained | Unknown whether the Suggested sidebar can expose private channel names | Before launch run the "Suggested sidebar test" in the launch checklist against the support guild and record the result |

## 2. Purpose and positioning

Official Nxeon community: players and hosts talking to each other and to the team. It is NOT where customers get account support. Account, billing and server problems go through the portal ticket system (or the private support guild for linked customers). Say this in the rules, the welcome message and the listing.

Voice: Nxeon speaks as the owner. Never describe any third-party infrastructure vendor to the community.

Honesty rules for the community and the listing: no member counts, uptime figures, ratings, awards or customer numbers unless read from real data at the time of posting. The "47 seconds" tagline is brand copy and may be used as the tagline.

## 3. Guild separation

| | Community guild (NEW) | Support guild (existing "Nxeon Cloud") |
|---|---|---|
| Audience | Public, anyone aged 13+ (Discord minimum) | Staff, plus linked customers in their own ticket channel only |
| Contains | Welcome, Community, Games, Showcase, Voice, Help (peer to peer) | Staff HQ, Management, Meetings, ticket and live-chat categories, status alerts |
| Customer data | Never. No ticket mirror, no account lookup, no server lists | Yes, per ticket channel only |
| Bots | Moderation bot + community utilities (section 5) | The existing "Nxeon Support" HTTP bot |
| Invite | Public vanity or permanent invite on the website | Invite-only, short expiry, no public link anywhere |
| Listing on Disboard / top.gg | Yes | Never |

Changes that follow for the support guild (do these before the community launch is promoted):

1. Remove its public community categories (Welcome, Community, Support self-help, Game Servers, Voice) once their content has moved. Keep Alerts staff-only.
2. Set verification level to the highest the staff can live with, enable 2FA requirement for moderation actions, and turn off "Allow members to see Suggested channels" behaviour as far as Discord allows (see V8 test).
3. Hide the guild from Server Discovery and from any listing.
4. Keep the explicit `@everyone` deny on every ticket, live-chat and archived category (already in `createGuildTextChannel`/`createGuildCategory`).

Nothing in the repo is changed by this blueprint. The wiring options (D1, D3 in section 10) are owner decisions.

## 4. Roles and permissions

Principle: roles are few, named by what they can do, and the highest-risk permissions sit with the fewest people. Role order top to bottom is also the hierarchy order in Discord.

| Order | Role | Who | Notable permissions |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Owner | Owner only | Administrator is used ONLY on this role. Hold it on a personal account with 2FA, not on any bot |
| 2 | Bot: Moderation | The moderation bot | Manage Roles (below it only), Kick, Ban, Moderate Members, Manage Messages, View Audit Log. No Administrator |
| 3 | Bot: Utility | Welcome/utility bots | Send Messages, Embed Links, Manage Roles only if reaction roles are used, Manage Threads. Nothing else |
| 4 | Admin | Trusted senior moderator (optional) | Manage Channels, Manage Messages, Kick, Ban, Moderate Members. NOT Manage Server, NOT Manage Webhooks, NOT Administrator |
| 5 | Moderator | Volunteers, after trial period | Manage Messages, Moderate Members (timeout), Kick; Ban only after trial. No Mention Everyone |
| 6 | Nxeon Team | Staff showing as official | Cosmetic and channel-access role, hoisted, no extra powers. Used so members can tell the team from impostors |
| 7 | Verified Customer | Linked Nxeon customers (optional, decision D3) | Unlocks #customers-lounge. Cosmetic otherwise |
| 8 | Partner / Creator | Creator partners (optional, decision D3) | Access to #creators; cosmetic otherwise |
| 9 | Server Owner (game roles) | Self-assigned game roles from onboarding | Only controls which game channels a member sees. Never grants permissions |
| 10 | Member | Everyone who passes the rules screen | Default posting rights |
| 11 | @everyone | Before rules screen | View Channel on #welcome, #rules, #announcements only. No Send Messages, no Add Reactions, no Create Invite, no Embed Links, no Attach Files, no external emoji, no Mention Everyone |

Hard rules for the permission model:

- Mention Everyone / Mention All Roles is denied for every role except Owner and the announcements bot. This closes the classic "@everyone scam" path.
- Create Invite is denied for @everyone and Member. Invites come from the owner and the website only.
- Manage Webhooks, Manage Server and Manage Guild Expressions are Owner-only.
- Every moderator and admin must have 2FA on their Discord account. Turn on "Require 2FA for moderation" in Server Settings > Safety Setup. This is also a prerequisite for Server Discovery.
- No role is granted from a Discord message, a bot command by a non-staff user, or a link. Role changes come from onboarding, from the badge sync, or from the Owner.
- Moderators never receive customer data. If a member posts account details, moderators delete the message and point to the portal ticket.

## 5. Channel structure

Names are lowercase with hyphens. Slowmode values are defaults to tune after launch. "Read only" means members have View Channel and Read Message History but no Send Messages.

### Category: START HERE (read only for everyone)
- `#welcome`: what Nxeon is in two sentences, the tagline, links to the website, status page and docs, the role-picker prompt. Read only.
- `#rules`: the rules text from section 8, read only. Required for Community and for the rules screen.
- `#announcements`: product news and changes. Announcement channel, read only, posted by the Nxeon Team. Followable by other servers.
- `#get-roles`: onboarding fallback; reaction or button roles for games and notification pings. Read only apart from the buttons.
- `#faq`: short answers and links to /docs and /help. Read only.

### Category: COMMUNITY
- `#general`: open chat. Slowmode 5 seconds. No links for new members for the first 10 minutes (AutoMod rule).
- `#introductions`: say hello, what you play or host.
- `#showcase`: servers, builds, screenshots, clips. Image and link posting allowed. One post per thread rule: replies go in threads (auto-thread on).
- `#off-topic`: everything else, still under the rules.
- `#suggestions`: product ideas, one idea per post, bot-managed upvotes. Feeds the owner's improvement process, but members are told ideas are read, not promised.

### Category: LOOKING FOR GROUP (one channel per game; only visible to members who picked the game in onboarding)
Create a channel only when the game has real Nxeon demand. Start from games the platform already hosts as top families (Minecraft, Valheim, Rust, Palworld, CS2, Terraria, Project Zomboid, ARK, others added later):
- `#lfg-minecraft`, `#lfg-valheim`, `#lfg-rust`, `#lfg-palworld`, `#lfg-cs2`, `#lfg-terraria`, `#lfg-other`.
- Pinned post per channel: how to ask for a group ("game, region, time zone, mods, age range if relevant"). No advertising of paid third-party servers or other hosting companies.
- Slowmode 30 seconds to stop LFG spam.

### Category: PATCH AND NEWS
- `#patch-news`: game patch notes and Rust wipe dates, posted by a human or an approved bot. Read only. Mirrors the playbook output in `docs/PLAYBOOK-PATCH-DAY-AND-RUST-WIPE.md` after human approval. No automated post from the platform.
- `#nxeon-status`: a read-only feed of the PUBLIC status page incidents (manual posts or an RSS feed bot pointed at the public status URL). Never the internal `discord_status_alerts_channel_id` feed, which stays in the staff guild.
- `#wipe-calendar`: pinned dates for force wipes (Rust first Thursday, about 19:00 UTC), with a reminder that dates are confirmed with the publisher.

### Category: HELP (peer to peer, NOT account support)
- `#help-hosting`: members help each other with server setup questions. A pinned banner says: "Account, billing, payment and server-down problems: open a ticket in your Nxeon dashboard. Never post passwords, API keys, IPs of private servers or payment details here."
- `#help-mods-and-plugins`: modding and plugin questions.
- `#bug-reports`: structured form (thread template: what you did, what happened, game, server region). Staff triage; confirmed items go to the board by a staff member.
- Forum channel option: use a Forum channel for `#help-hosting` so each question is a tagged post (tags: setup, mods, network, billing-redirect, solved). Moderators close solved posts.

### Category: VOICE
- `Lounge`, `Gaming 1`, `Gaming 2`, `Events`. Push-to-talk not enforced. Voice text channel gets slowmode. Stage channel `Community call` for the occasional town hall.

### Category: CUSTOMERS (only if decision D3 is yes)
- `#customers-lounge`: visible to Verified Customer role. Casual chat only; still no account data.

1. Joins and sees only `#welcome`, `#rules`, `#announcements` (the @everyone view from section 4).
2. Accepts the rules screen. The Member role is granted on acceptance.
3. Answers onboarding question 1, "What do you play or host?" (multi-select, optional): maps to game roles that unlock the matching `#lfg-*` channels.
4. Answers onboarding question 2, "What are you here for?" (single-select, optional): "Finding a group", "Hosting my own server", "Showing my server", "Just looking". Each option opens a sensible channel set. No option grants a privileged role.
5. Answers onboarding question 3, "Which announcements do you want?" (multi-select): `Patch news`, `Rust wipe`, `Nxeon updates`. These are ping roles used sparingly.

2. Keep it legal and fair. No piracy, cheats-for-sale, account trading, doxxing or anything that breaks a game's terms.
3. No scams, spam or self-promotion. No unsolicited DMs, invite links, affiliate links, crypto or giveaway offers. Showcasing your own server is welcome in `#showcase` only.
4. No advertising other hosting companies or paid servers.
5. Never share passwords, API keys, tokens, payment details or private server logins. Nxeon staff will never ask for them in a message. Anyone who does is an impostor: report them.

Needs a code change: a separate setting for the join target (for example `discord_community_guild_id`) and keeping `discordGuildId()` for the support bridge. Recommended yes, and the support guild invite-only afterwards.

## 11. Success measures (for the owner to read from real data later)

Do not set numeric targets in public. Track privately: joins, retention at 7 and 30 days, messages per active member, moderation actions per week, tickets mistakenly opened in the community (should be zero), signups with a Discord UTM (see launch checklist). Report only what is measured.

# Nxeon community Discord: server blueprint (mkt-036)

Status: DESIGN ONLY. Nothing in this document has been created on Discord, Disboard or top.gg. The owner (or a person the owner delegates) builds it by hand from this blueprint using the launch checklist in `docs/COMMUNITY-DISCORD-LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md`, and the listing text is in `docs/COMMUNITY-DISCORD-LISTING-COPY.md`.

Owner decision (growth batch, 2026-10-02): `change`. The owner's words: "We have a discord. However our discord community is super basic. I feel like it needs some work. Currently there are vulnerabilities, and it's just too basic. Needs more advancement."

So this is not a greenfield server. It is a rebuild of the community side, with the security problems designed out first.

## 1. What exists today, and why it must be split

Facts below come from the repo (`lib/discord*.ts`, `lib/settings.ts`) and the incident notes for 2026-09-05 and 2026-09-06.

- One Discord guild, "Nxeon Cloud", does three unrelated jobs at once: staff HQ and management, per-customer support ticket and live-chat channels (created by `lib/discord-bridge.ts`), and a public community area (Welcome, Community, Support self-help, Game Servers, Voice, Alerts).
- The bot ("Nxeon Support") is HTTP-only (Interactions Endpoint, REST). It is not a Gateway client, so it cannot moderate, welcome, or react to joins. It holds the Administrator permission.
- "Sign in with Discord" requests the `guilds.join` scope and adds every customer who signs up that way straight into that same guild (`lib/discord-auth.ts`, `app/api/discord/login/route.ts`). Customers are therefore auto-joined into the guild that contains staff and ticket channels.
- Customer badge roles (Verified, VPS Owner, Game Owner, Hosting, Partner) are synced from real account data by `lib/discord-roles.ts`. Staff roles (Owner, Admin, Manager, Staff, Customer Support) are assigned by hand.
- 2026-09-05: ticket and live-chat channels were visible to non-staff members because categories were created with no `@everyone` deny. Fixed in code and live. 2026-09-06: a narrower recurrence was reported (a fresh account saw one ticket channel name in the Suggested sidebar) and is recorded as unresolved.

### Vulnerability list this rebuild must close

| # | Weakness | Why it matters | Fix in this design |
|---|---|---|---|
| V1 | Community and customer tickets share one guild | Any permission slip exposes private support data; the 2026-09-05 leak happened exactly this way | Two guilds. Community is a new guild with NO ticket channels and NO customer data. Tickets stay in the existing guild, which becomes private (see section 3) |
| V2 | Auto-join of every Discord-signup customer into the support guild | Customers land in the staff guild by default | Owner decision D1: point auto-join at the community guild, and make the support guild invite-only. Needs a small code change, NOT made here |
| V3 | Bot has Administrator | A stolen bot token is full server takeover | Community guild bot set uses least-privilege roles (section 5). Support bot: replace Administrator with the specific permissions it uses (Manage Channels, Manage Roles, Send Messages, View Channel, Read Message History, Embed Links), tested on a spare guild first |
| V4 | No moderation layer (HTTP-only bot cannot see joins or messages) | Raids, scams, invite spam, token-grabber links | A real moderation bot plus Discord's own AutoMod (section 6). The HTTP bot stays out of the community |
| V5 | Basic setup: no verification level, no rules screen, no onboarding | Throwaway accounts can post immediately | Community feature on, rules screen, verification level, onboarding questions (sections 4 and 7) |
| V6 | Staff roles can be assigned in the Discord UI by anyone with Manage Roles | Role escalation | Only Owner holds Manage Roles; moderators get a capped role below the bot's role; 2FA required for every moderator (section 4) |
| V7 | Webhook and invite sprawl | Leaked webhook = posting as the server | Quarterly audit of webhooks, integrations and invites (checklist) |
| V8 | Open recurrence from 2026-09-06 is unexplained | Unknown whether the Suggested sidebar can expose private channel names | Before launch run the "Suggested sidebar test" in the launch checklist against the support guild and record the result |

## 2. Purpose and positioning

Official Nxeon community: players and hosts talking to each other and to the team. It is NOT where customers get account support. Account, billing and server problems go through the portal ticket system (or the private support guild for linked customers). Say this in the rules, the welcome message and the listing.

Voice: Nxeon speaks as the owner. Never describe any third-party infrastructure vendor to the community.

Honesty rules for the community and the listing: no member counts, uptime figures, ratings, awards or customer numbers unless read from real data at the time of posting. The "47 seconds" tagline is brand copy and may be used as the tagline.

## 3. Guild separation

| | Community guild (NEW) | Support guild (existing "Nxeon Cloud") |
|---|---|---|
| Audience | Public, anyone aged 13+ (Discord minimum) | Staff, plus linked customers in their own ticket channel only |
| Contains | Welcome, Community, Games, Showcase, Voice, Help (peer to peer) | Staff HQ, Management, Meetings, ticket and live-chat categories, status alerts |
| Customer data | Never. No ticket mirror, no account lookup, no server lists | Yes, per ticket channel only |
| Bots | Moderation bot + community utilities (section 5) | The existing "Nxeon Support" HTTP bot |
| Invite | Public vanity or permanent invite on the website | Invite-only, short expiry, no public link anywhere |
| Listing on Disboard / top.gg | Yes | Never |

import { classifyEmailDomain, emailDomain, checkEligibility, type ClubInput } from "../lib/club-programme";

});

  assert.equal(checkEligibility({ ...clan, memberCount: null }, NOW).ok, false);
  assert.equal(checkEligibility({ ...clan, memberCount: 5 }, NOW).ok, true);
});

  assert.equal(checkEligibility({ ...lan, eventStart: d("2027-06-01"), eventEnd: d("2027-06-02") }, NOW).ok, false); // too far
});

  assert.equal(r.ok, true);

});

*
 * Pure and dependency-free: no SSH, no clock. Covered by test/game-update.test.ts,
 * which also runs `sh -n` and `dash -n` over the generated script.
 */

/**
 * Steam dedicated-server app IDs for families whose game files are updated by
 * steamcmd running DIRECTLY ON THE HOST, next to a systemd unit that manages the
 * server process itself (not a container).
 *
 * valheim/rust/palworld/cs2 were REMOVED from this table 2026-09-10, found live
 * via a real customer's Valheim server (`terraheim`) failing its GAME_UPDATE job
 * on every single run for 2 days straight with "steamcmd is not installed" —
 * true, but not fixable, because all four are actually Docker-run
 * (`OsTemplate.setupScript` installs Docker and `docker run`s an image; a thin
 * systemd unit wraps it as `ExecStart=docker start -a <name>` purely so the rest
 * of the platform can treat it like any other service). steamcmd for these lives
 * inside the container's own image, if it exists at all — never on the host —
 * so `command -v steamcmd` on the host can never succeed, and the job was
 * pointlessly retrying and re-notifying the customer every ~6h/24h forever for
 * 5 real live servers (3 valheim, 1 rust, 1 palworld) with zero chance of ever
 * resolving. This is the exact bug class already fixed for waves 3/4/8/9 and
 * the Plutonium family below — those all correctly stayed OUT of this table
 * from the start; these four just predate that convention and were never
 * migrated onto it until now. Restart-only (via the wrapper unit, confirmed
 * live to correctly call `docker start -a`/`docker stop`) is what these get
 * instead — see `updatesFromSteam()`.
 */
export const STEAM_APPID: Partial<Record<GameFamily, string>> = {};

/** systemd service name candidates per family (first that exists wins). */
export const SERVICE_HINT: Record<GameFamily, string> = {
  minecraft: "minecraft",
  valheim: "valheim",
  rust: "rust",
  palworld: "palworld",
  cs2: "cs2",
  terraria: "terraria",
  ark: "ark",
  satisfactory: "satisfactory",
  projectzomboid: "projectzomboid",
  sdtd: "sdtd",
  vrising: "vrising",
  enshrouded: "enshrouded",
  factorio: "factorio",
  gmod: "gmod",
  conan: "conan",
  unturned: "unturned",
  theforest: "theforest",
  sonsoftheforest: "sonsoftheforest",
  bedrock: "bedrock",
  // ── Wave 3 SCAFFOLD (2026-08-31). Kept OUT of STEAM_APPID on purpose: without a
  //    Steam app id these families are "restart-only" for the auto-update job (never
1048:  autoUpdate            Boolean             @default(false) // game-server auto-update opt-in
3727:  autoUpdate         String?
7009:  autoUpdateLocked Boolean   @default(false) // admin override: customer cannot change Server.autoUpdate

# Game patch-day and Rust wipe-day playbooks (mkt-026)

Owner decision: `do`. Agent-assisted, human-approved. This document is the playbook; the machine-readable checklist templates are in `lib/game-playbooks.ts`, and `/admin/playbooks` opens them as tasks on the staff "Game operations" board.

Hard rule: NOTHING here sends anything to a customer automatically. Every customer-facing artefact (announcement, email, help article, status post, Discord post) is produced as a DRAFT and sent by a human. The only automation is internal: a staff task with a checklist, and an admin notification.

## What exists in the platform today (read before promising anything)

- Per-game auto-update: `Server.autoUpdate` (default off, customer opt-in; admin can lock it). `worker/game-update.ts` `gameUpdateSweep` runs every 6 hours and queues `GAME_UPDATE` jobs. The outcome is judged by `lib/game-update-verify.ts`, not by a clean exit code.
- Honest limit for Docker-run families (Valheim, Rust, Palworld, CS2): `STEAM_APPID` is empty for them, so the update job is restart-only through the wrapper unit (`docker start -a`). Whether a restart picks up the new game build depends on the image. Never tell customers "we update your Rust server automatically" unless a staging test has just proven a restart picks up the new build. Prove it on a throwaway server first (checklist item).
- Danger Zone "Wipe & reinstall" (`reinstallGame`) exists for customers, behind typed confirmation `WIPE`. It destroys the world. It is a customer action; staff never trigger it on a customer's behalf for a wipe-day.
- Rust RCON is WebSocket (`rcon.web`) and is not wired into the generic control path (`lib/game-control.ts` says deferred). Do not plan around staff running Rust RCON commands fleet-wide.
- Admin Notification (`notifyAdmins`, `worker/monitor.ts`) and WorkTask/WorkChecklistItem exist and are what the hooks use.
- Rust map wipes: the server's world size/seed settings are in the Rust config schema (`lib/game-config.ts`). Changing worldsize regenerates the map on the next wipe.

## Roles

- Owner: approves every customer-facing draft.
- Operator (human on duty): works the checklist, runs the test server, sends approved messages.
- Agent: watches sources, drafts, files the evidence on the task. The agent never sends, never changes a customer server, never runs a job against a customer server.

## Playbook A: Rust force wipe (first Thursday, about 19:00 UTC)

Calendar (calculated by `upcomingRustWipes`, confirm each against the publisher's schedule when the checklist opens):
- 2026-11-05 19:00 UTC
- 2026-12-03 19:00 UTC
- then the first Thursday of each month.

Timeline (the checklist template mirrors this):
- T-48h, automatic when the flag is on: the worker opens the checklist task and notifies admins. Operator confirms the date, lists Rust customers, checks node capacity, runs the staging test server, reviews the help article.
- T-24h: the agent drafts (a) a customer notice for the in-portal announcement and an optional email, (b) a status-page maintenance note, (c) canned support replies. All drafts only. Owner approves.
- T-2h: operator pins the canned replies and reviews open Rust tickets.
- T-0: operator watches `GAME_UPDATE` jobs and Rust server status. Failures are investigated by hand.
- T+1h: spot-check three real customer Rust servers.
- T+24h: review tickets and failed jobs; update this playbook and `/admin/docs` with anything learned.

Customer notice draft skeleton (the agent fills the date, a human checks every sentence):
> Rust's monthly update and force wipe lands on [date, time UTC]. After it, your server needs to run the new game version so players can connect. [Only if proven: restarting your server from the dashboard will pick up the update.] Your files and settings are kept unless you choose to wipe. If you want a fresh map, use [the wipe option] after the update. Questions: open a ticket from your dashboard.

Do not write "automatic" unless it is proven that day. Do not give a player count, an ETA or a discount.

## Playbook B: game patch day

Trigger: a human (or the agent's suggestion confirmed by a human) decides that a publisher patch matters for a game Nxeon customers run. Start from `/admin/playbooks`: pick the game and open the checklist (once per game per UTC day).

Steps (mirrors `PATCH_DAY_ITEMS`):
1. Confirm the patch from the publisher's own notes; record the link.
2. Decide impact: does it break client compatibility.
3. Check whether the family's update path is wired and say so honestly (see limits above).
4. Check mods and plugin frameworks for incompatibility before telling anyone to update.
5. Prove the update on one internal server using the update verifier's output.
6. Draft the same-day guide as a draft article (these guides also feed the SEO and answer-engine content plan; see `docs/SEO-AUDIT-2026-10.md`).
7. Draft the customer notice for people running that game. Owner approves, a human sends.
8. After release review failed jobs and tickets.

Agent brief (run as a normal agent task, read-only against the platform):
- Inputs: the publisher's official patch-notes page or the game's public RSS/announcement feed for the top families by active servers. Read-only web reads. No logins.
- Output: a markdown draft per patch containing source link, what changed in plain words, who is affected, recommended customer action, and the checklist link. Saved as a draft article or attached to the task. No sends.
- The agent states any uncertainty ("not confirmed by the publisher") in the draft. It never invents version numbers, dates or player numbers.

## Wording and brand rules for drafts

- Nxeon speaks as the owner. Never name or imply a third-party infrastructure vendor.
- No fabricated statistics, reviews or customer counts.
- The "47 seconds" tagline is intentional brand copy; do not change or flag it.
- Hytale and FiveM are legally sensitive; this playbook covers neither. Informational mentions only, no managed-hosting promises.
- Marketing emails must respect opt-outs; a service-impact notice about a customer's own server is a transactional-style message, but the choice of kind and recipients is the owner's, so it stays a draft.

## Enabling the hooks

- Settings > Programmes > "Open Rust wipe-day checklists automatically" (`game_playbooks_enabled`, default off; env `GAME_PLAYBOOKS_ENABLED=true` also enables it). Worker job name `game-playbooks`, hourly. Idempotent: the task description carries `[playbook:rust-wipe-YYYY-MM-DD]` and a second run is a no-op.
- `/admin/playbooks` (platform area) works whether or not the flag is on: calendar, manual open buttons, recent tasks.
- Tasks appear on the "Game operations" board in `/admin/tasks` (created on first use).

## Owner decisions / open items

- Which families get patch-day coverage first. Suggested order follows active customer servers; read the real counts from `/admin/games`.
- Whether a restart-only update path is acceptable to describe to customers once the staging proof exists, or a real image-pull update step should be built for Docker families. That is separate engineering, not part of this item.
- Approval workflow for customer notices (who signs off, and the channel).
E

cd /opt/nxeon-wt-g7/docs; cat > PROGRAMME-CLUBS-CLANS-LAN.md <<'E'
# School club, clan and LAN programme (mkt-041)

Owner decision: `do`. Item write-up: "A free or discounted server for verified school or university clubs (staff email) and for LAN or esports events, with a co-branded join page and a code for members. Conversion evidence is UNVERIFIED, so run it as a time-boxed test with 5-10 clubs in SG, PH and MY." Recommended flag in the write-up: not recommended by default, so it ships OFF.

No discount number is invented in this document or in the code. Every value comes from the existing discount mechanics below; anything that would be a NEW money rule is listed under "Owner decisions".

## What was built

| Piece | Where | State |
|---|---|---|
| Public page | `app/(marketing)/clubs/page.tsx` -> `/clubs` | Returns 404 until `club_programme_enabled` is on |
| Application form | `components/marketing/ClubApplyForm.tsx`, action `submitClubApplication` in `lib/actions-club.ts` | Stores the application only. No email, no coupon, no charge, no Discord post |
| Eligibility rules | `lib/club-programme.ts` (pure, tested) | Rules below |
| Storage | Prisma model `ClubApplication` (additive, no relations) | New table; applied by the normal additive `db push` |
| Review queue | `/admin/club-applications` (platform area) | Admin sets status, internal note, and records the coupon code they issued |
| Switch | Settings > Programmes > `club_programme_enabled` (default off) | Off |

Spam and abuse controls: honeypot field, per-connection rate limit (5 per 10 minutes), one open application per email and group type, server-side validation of every field, no IP stored, internal admin notification only.

## Eligibility rules (proposed defaults, owner can change the constants in `lib/club-programme.ts`)

These are not money rules.

- School or university club: must name the institution; must apply from a staff or school email, free webmail addresses (Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, iCloud and similar) are refused; an email domain that does not look institutional is accepted but flagged for the reviewer. The domain check is a HINT, never proof: a reviewer confirms the club exists on the institution's own website or through its own switchboard before approval.
- Clan or community team: at least 5 members.
- LAN or esports event: venue or organiser named; start and end dates required; application at least 7 days and at most 180 days before the start; event no longer than 14 days (longer is a custom enquiry).
- Region: the test runs in Singapore, the Philippines and Malaysia first. Other countries can apply and are queued, flagged "outside pilot".
- One open application per email per group type. A person reviews every application; there is no auto-approval.
- Age: applications come from a staff member, an organiser or an adult club lead. Minors do not open accounts through this form.
- Abuse: reviewer may revoke an approved arrangement for resale, cryptomining, or using it for something other than the stated group.

## The offer, expressed in existing mechanics only

An approved group gets ONE of the following, chosen by the owner per group. Values stay blank here on purpose.

1. Member discount code (the "code for members" in the item). Create it in Admin > Coupons (`Coupon`). Existing knobs: `kind` (PERCENT, FIXED_CENTS, CREDIT_CENTS, or the flat first-term-price kind), `value`, `serviceKind` (GAME or VPS), `planSlug` (lock to one plan), `maxTermMonths` (cap how many months of a term are discounted so it cannot be stretched), `maxRedemptions`, `expiresAt`, `firstTimeOnly`, `excludeActiveCustomers`, and the built-in one-per-account and one-per-IP redemption limits. Recorded on the application in `couponCode`.
2. A single free server for the group, using Admin > Grant a free VPS (`Server.isFree`, no billing, `expiresAt` null). This is a manual comp, not a self-service flow. For game servers a time-limited arrangement can instead use the existing partner free-server grant (`PartnerGrant`, with 7-day and 1-day expiry notices) but that requires the group lead to be a partner record; that is a separate owner decision.
3. A wallet credit via a gift code (Admin > Gift codes) in an amount the owner picks.

Because coupons are one per account, a group code works as "each member gets the discount once" (the cap is `maxRedemptions`). A single shared server for the whole club is option 2.

Commission: a coupon issued here does not create referral commission. If the group lead should ALSO be a creator partner, that goes through the separate Creator Partner Program and its own terms.

## Co-branded join page

The item asks for a co-branded join page. Built as the public `/clubs` page for applications. A per-club page (club name and logo on a page with the member code) is NOT built: it needs a design decision about whose logo may be shown, and a verified-club check before any third-party name appears on Nxeon's site. Proposed next step after the first approvals: a static page per approved club, created by hand, reviewed by the owner.

## Operating procedure (human)

1. Turn on `club_programme_enabled` only after the owner decisions below are made.
2. Applications arrive in Admin > Club applications; admins also get an in-portal notification.
3. Reviewer verifies the group independently (institution website, event page, club social page), sets NEEDS_INFO or APPROVED or REJECTED, writes an internal note.
4. If approved: create the coupon (or grant) using the owner's values, paste the code into the row, reply to the contact by normal email from the support mailbox, then save the status.
5. Keep the test small: 5 to 10 groups total, as the item says. Record outcome per group (did members sign up, did anyone pay) in the internal note. Decide to continue, change or stop after the time box.

## Measuring the test honestly

Real data only: applications received, approved, members who redeemed the code (coupon `timesRedeemed` and `CouponRedemption` rows), paid servers that followed. The write-up marks conversion evidence UNVERIFIED, so report what is measured, nothing projected.

## Owner decisions needed (nothing here is invented)

- O1. The actual offer per group type: which of options 1 to 3, and the numbers (`value`, `maxTermMonths`, `maxRedemptions`, `expiresAt`, plan lock). Any figure is a NEW money rule and has to come from the owner. The public page deliberately states no numbers.
- O2. Cost cap for the test: how many comped servers or how much total discount the owner will fund. Capacity is internal, but a free server still occupies a node slot.
- O3. Whether eligibility constants (5 members, 7 to 180 days, 14-day events) are right.
- O4. Whether the public page should be linked from the footer and added to the sitemap (`lib/sitemap-sections.ts`) at launch. Not done, so a flag-off 404 never appears in a sitemap.
- O5. Who answers applications and from which mailbox, and the reply time promise (the public page makes none).
- O6. Whether a per-club co-branded page is wanted and the rules for using a school's name or logo.
- O7. Whether students under 18 may be members of an approved club server (the form is for staff and organisers only).

## Safety and legal notes

- No claim about any school's endorsement, no testimonial and no member count appears anywhere. Nxeon speaks as the owner; no third-party infrastructure vendor is named.
- Hytale and FiveM are legally sensitive. This programme is informational and game-agnostic; an application naming FiveM or Hytale is answered by a human and no managed offer is made without the owner's permission.
- Personal data stored: name, email, role, institution, country, member count, free text. No IP, no account is created. Review and delete rejected applications on a regular schedule; add the retention period to the privacy policy review (owner).
E

- `docs/COMMUNITY-DISCORD-LISTING-COPY.md` has the Disboard, top.gg and Discovery copy with no invented stats. `docs/COMMUNITY-DISCORD-LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md` is the step-by-step launch list.

- The blueprint therefore proposes a separate community guild with no ticket bot and no customer data, and an invite-only support guild.

- `docs/PLAYBOOK-PATCH-DAY-AND-RUST-WIPE.md` is the playbook.
- `lib/game-playbooks.ts` holds the wipe calendar and checklist templates. Rust wipes are the first Thursday at 19:00 UTC, so 2026-11-05 and 2026-12-03.
- `lib/game-playbooks-tasks.ts` creates one task per wipe or patch, with its checklist, on a "Game operations" work board. It is idempotent.

- `/admin/playbooks` shows the calendar and has manual buttons for the next Rust wipe and for a per-game patch day.
- Nothing sends to customers; customer-facing messages stay drafts.
- Docker-run games, including Rust, are restart-only for auto-update. The playbook says not to promise an automatic update without a staging test.

- `lib/actions-club.ts` handles the public submit, which only stores the application. It has a honeypot, a rate limit and one open application per email and group type. No IP is stored.

- `/admin/club-applications` is the review queue. An admin sets the status and records a coupon code they issued separately.
- Discounts must come from the existing Coupon, Grant or Gift-code mechanics. The numbers are left as owner decisions.

- Deploy needs the additive `prisma db push` for `ClubApplication`.
